subject: history_social
passage: The Black Death, which swept across Europe between 1347 and 1351, killed perhaps a third or more of the continent's population. In England, the surviving laborers found themselves in demand: despite laws that tried to hold wages at preplague levels, pay rose, and over the following century serfdom largely disappeared. Economic historian Signe Dahl draws a general lesson from this outcome. When labor becomes scarce, she argues, the bargaining power of workers inevitably rises and the bonds of servitude weaken.
passage_b: Demographic shock alone cannot explain what happened next, because the shock did not produce the same result everywhere. In parts of eastern Europe, where labor was also in short supply, landowners responded over the following two centuries by tying peasants more firmly to their estates, a development historians call the "second serfdom." Whether scarcity empowered workers seems to have depended on whether lords were organized and strong enough to restrict peasants' movement.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the general lesson drawn by Dahl in Text 1?

choices.A: By suggesting that laws limiting wages worked far better in eastern Europe than they did in England
choices.B: By claiming that serfdom in England survived the plague largely unchanged
choices.C: By rejecting the idea that the plague had any lasting effect on European laborers
choices.D: By pointing to a case in which labor scarcity led to stronger rather than weaker servitude

explanation.why: Dahl claims that scarce labor "inevitably" strengthens workers and weakens servitude. Text 2 describes eastern Europe, "where labor was also in short supply," yet landowners tied peasants "more firmly to their estates." That single counterexample shows the outcome was not inevitable but depended on the power of lords.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 credits lords' power to restrict peasants' movement, not wage laws.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 does not challenge Text 1's account of England; it adds a contrasting case from eastern Europe.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says the plague's effects differed by region, not that it had no lasting effect.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2's account of the "second serfdom" in eastern Europe is a case where scarcity was followed by harsher, not looser, servitude.
